body: Quick pass: merges cleanly with main; body complete; author's quick gate green on 81e4cb01 (pins in `lathe_workholding_live.rs` and `lathe_workholding_rpm.rs`); no post script touched. Flagged ready; a spindle-limit rule, so it gets the high-tier review.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 81e4cb015d0ae9e6daf4c549726fcf3001e1359e -->
**Needs changes before merge** (high-tier review: safety limit at the program gate)

### What I built, ran and tried
Head 81e4cb01 trial-merged with origin/main 0fc30b65 (clean, no conflicts; local only, never pushed).

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| lathe_workholding_live | 3 passed |
| lathe_workholding_rpm | 6 passed |
| mcp_workholding | 1 passed |
| lathe_spindle_law | 8 passed |
| lathe_post | 7 passed |
| lathe_post_css | 10 passed |
| c_axis_live | 5 passed |
| c_axis_unwind | 7 passed |
| operations | 117 passed, 6 ignored |
| golden_cl | 25 passed (goldens untouched) |
| project_roundtrip | 71 passed |
| clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings | clean |

Plus throwaway local probes (deleted, not committed): an on-centre Drill on a lathe and on a mill-turn, and a cross drill on a mill-turn, each posted through `fanuc-lathe.cps` with `posting::post_script` (the full gate + post).

### Requested before merge
1. **A mill-turn's on-centre Drill spins the work at the drill's rpm and is not judged - it posts.** `crates/app/src/setup_workholding.rs:102` (`work_speed`) falls back to `spindle_law::turns`, which is true for a Drill only on `Kind::Lathe` (or a mill-turn *cross* drill, `spindle_law.rs:248-250`). A Drill with axial holes on a `mill-turn` setup therefore lands in `WorkSpeed::Not`. But the post does not care which kind the machine is: `fanuc-lathe.cps:424` opens every section without `PARAM LiveTool` with `G97 S<rpm> M03`, the work spindle. Reproduction (revolved Ø12 bar with a blind Ø4.4 centre hole, Drill op with one `Hole` at XY 0,0, DR-0400 at 8000 rpm, Setup1 workholding max 2000 rpm):
   - machine `kind: "lathe"`: gate refuses `D1: turns the work at 8000 rpm (G97), over setup 'Setup1''s workholding maximum of 2000 rpm ...` - correct.
   - machine `kind: "mill-turn"`, same everything: `verification_gate` is empty and `post_script` returns **Ok**; the program reads
     ```
     T0101
     G50 S12000
     G97 S8000 M03
     M8
     G00 X0 Z16
     G83 Z6 Q12000 F0.01
     ```
     i.e. the chuck at 8000 rpm under a 2000 rpm rating.
   This was not judged on main either (so not a regression), but it is the exact dangerous direction this PR exists to settle, the function is being rewritten here, and #1190's "most milling paths leave the meridian, so this may be latent" does not hold: a drill (any on-centre canned cycle) never leaves the meridian. The decision file's own principle ("read from what the lathe post does with the section, not from the kind's name") points at the fix: on a setup whose machine is a lathe or mill-turn, every section with **no C move** and **not a cross drill** is `Stated` (the post gives its S to the work spindle), whatever its family; the `turns()` fallback should go. Please pin it with the mill-turn axial-drill case above (refused at 8000, allowed at the limit), and update the decision file's table row "Lathe Drill, axial holes" / "Everything else" and #1190 accordingly (or fold #1190 into this PR).

### Per-`OpType` table (fanuc-lathe.cps on a lathe / mill-turn setup)
| Kind(s) | Spindle the post gives S to | Judged by the gate after this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Facing, ProfileRough/Finish, GrooveRough/Finish, Part, Threading, Chamfering, TaperTurning, MultiPassTurning, FormTurning, BoringTurning (Turn family) | work (`G97 S M03` / `G96`) | yes - G97 rpm refused above the limit (pinned, at-the-limit allowed); G96 clamp min(machine, tool, chuck) unchanged (pins pass) |
| Drill, axial holes, `lathe` machine | work (`G97 S M03`, G83) | yes, stated rpm (probe confirmed) |
| **Drill, axial holes, `mill-turn` machine** | **work (`G97 S8000 M03`)** | **no - posts (blocker 1)** |
| Drill, cross holes (lathe or mill-turn) | post opens `G97 S M03` then refuses the posed B90 moves (`posed move ... no rotary to command`); machine gate also refuses (no B axis) | no (Not) - cannot post today, so safe; if a post ever voices posed cross drills the work-held claim needs re-checking |
| RotaryContour / RotaryParallel / RotaryOffset and any path stating C (`PARAM LiveTool`) | live spindle word + S; work on C | yes, by max(C feed, C rapid)/360 vs the limit; no C rate -> refused by name (pinned) |
| Bore, Circular, Thread (mill), Tapping-style cycles on centre, Probe, other Mill2D/3D kinds without C on a mill-turn | work (`G97 S M03`) whenever their moves stay on the meridian (an on-centre bore cycle does) | no - same hole as blocker 1; not probed individually |
| Multi-axis 5D kinds | posed A/B -> refused by the lathe post | n/a |

### Checked and holding
- C rate: reads the machine's C `feed`/`rapid` (deg/min, as `millturn.mch` states 6000/12000; no shipped `.mch` states C in rpm), filters non-finite and <= 0, takes the larger - so a C rewind at the rapid (#860/#964) is covered; compared exactly (`rate / 360.0 > hold`), rounding only in the text. No C rate under a limit -> refused by name. The post itself caps G01 C by the feed (else rapid), so the gate's ceiling is the stricter reading.
- `None` limit: `of()` returns `None` and the loop `continue`s before classification - every program posts as before (golden_cl and lathe_post goldens unchanged).
- No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` in `setup_workholding.rs` (175 lines); refusal texts name operation, setup, speed and limit in plain English.
- Cross drill under a 100 rpm chuck: no workholding line (pinned) - the issue's done-means.

### Notes (not blocking)
- `work_speed` treats any `rotary.is_some()` move as C; on a mill-turn that is the post's own `LiveTool` test (`post/mod.rs:261`), so the two agree.
- The PR body ends `Fixes #1174` followed by the generated-by line; fine.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Review fix pushed (b0434952): the gate reads `post::section_spindle::of` - the same derivation `post::dump` uses for PARAM LiveTool and the pose words - so the `turns()` fallback is gone and every section the lathe post opens on the work spindle is judged, whatever its kind. Pinned by `lathe_workholding_kinds` (per-kind table, lathe and mill-turn; mill-turn on-centre Drill/Bore refused at 8000 under 2000, allowed at the limit). Quick gate green on b0434952. Still a draft.

**Needs changes before merge** (re-review of the delta from 81e4cb01; high tier)

The previous blocker is fixed: a mill-turn on-centre Drill at 8000 rpm under a 2000 rpm chuck is now refused by name, and is allowed at exactly 2000. One fail-open path remains, on the same rule.

### What I built, ran and tried
Head b0434952 trial-merged with origin/main d7e9a807 (clean; local only, never pushed). The PR-only diff against main is 7 files: `post/section_spindle.rs` (new), `post/mod.rs` (2 lines), `setup_workholding.rs`, three test suites and the decision file. **No golden or recorded stream is changed by the PR.**

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-post` (all 21 binaries + lib) | all pass (24 lib, recorded_streams 12, script_fanuc_lathe 15, script_tormach_lathe 11, every dialect 11, post_engine 33, ...) |
| lathe_workholding_kinds | 5 passed, 1 ignored (heavy lane, reason names it) |
| lathe_workholding_live / _rpm / mcp_workholding | 3 / 6 / 1 passed |
| lathe_spindle_law, lathe_post, lathe_post_css | 8 / 7 / 10 passed |
| c_axis_live, c_axis_unwind | 5 / 7 passed |
| recorded_post_streams, conformance, golden_cl, solid_law_goldens | 2 / 6 / 25 / 5 passed |
| operations, project_roundtrip | 117 (6 ignored) / 71 passed |
| clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings | clean |

**Is the stream byte-identical?** Yes, by reading as well as by the goldens. `LiveTool`: the old condition was `t.moves.iter().any(|m| m.rotary.is_some())` and `section_spindle::of(t) == LiveTool` tests exactly that, checked first. Pose words: the arm is `match (m.rotary, m.axis)`, `(None, Some(a))`, so the new `leans(m)` (`rotary.is_none() && axis.is_some_and(!is_vertical)`) is the old `!is_vertical(&a)` guard restated. No section gains or loses `LiveTool`.

### Requested before merge
1. **A lathe post on a setup whose machine is a mill (or no machine) spins the work over a stated chuck limit, and the gate skips it.** `crates/app/src/setup_workholding.rs`, `work_speed`: `if !matches!(kind_of_setup(..), Kind::Lathe | Kind::MillTurn) { return WorkSpeed::Not; }`. That keys on the machine kind, but what spins the work is the post that runs. `kind_of_setup` also defaults to `Kind::Mill` when no machine is loaded. Reproduction (throwaway local test): a revolved Ø12 bar with a Ø4.4 centre hole, Drill with one axial hole at XY 0,0, DR-0400 at 8000 rpm, Setup1 `SetSetupWorkholdingRpm(2000)`, then `posting::post_script` with each lathe post:
   - no machine loaded: gate `[]`, **fanuc-lathe POSTED** `G50 S12000` / `G97 S8000 M03`; **tormach-lathe POSTED** `G97 S8000 M3`.
   - machine `kind: "mill"`: the same, both posted.
   - `kind: "lathe"` / `"mill-turn"`: refused by name (correct).

   The state can be reached: the limit row stays on the Setups page whenever a limit is stated (`setup_workholding_row.rs:22`), so a setup that was a lathe, then remounted or unloaded, keeps its limit. Turning ops are then stopped by the family door, but any milling op that stays on the meridian (a drill) posts through the lathe post with the work spindle at the drill's rpm. Main had the same hole (`turns()` was false there too), so this is not a regression. It is still the fail-open direction this issue is about, and the guard is new code here. Two fixes, either one:
   - (a) While a limit is stated, judge `SectionSpindle::Work` sections whatever the machine kind. A limit stated means someone said there is a chuck. On a real mill this refuses too widely, which is the safe side, and the user can clear the limit.
   - (b) Judge by the post being a lathe post rather than by the machine kind.

   Pin it with the no-machine and mill-machine drill cases above.

### Classification attacks (all hold)
- **A/B equal to zero throughout:** `leans` needs a non-vertical axis, so a plain section written with a vertical axis is `Work` and judged. It cannot escape as `Posed`.
- **C stated on some moves only, or a constant C:** the section is `LiveTool`, judged by max(C feed, C rapid)/360. That is too strict for a C that never turns, which is the safe side.
- **Empty or rapids-only section:** `Work`, judged by the tool rpm (safe).
- **`Posed` is not judged:** both lathe posts refuse posed moves by name. `posed()` is checked first in fanuc-lathe's rapid, linear, circular and thread handlers, and in tormach-lathe at lines 443/452/548/636, ahead of `drillIgnore`. `dump` writes a Move record for every leaning move, so a posed section always reaches a refusal. My earlier probe of the B90 cross drill was refused by the post and by the machine gate.
- **Boundary:** a drill at exactly 2000 under 2000 is allowed. At 2000.4 it is refused, and the text then reads "2000 rpm ... over ... 2000 rpm" because of `{:.0}`. That is a cosmetic note: it fails closed, but a refusal whose two numbers look equal could confuse.
- **G96:** the clamp path is untouched (lathe_workholding_rpm pins pass). **No limit stated:** `of()` returns `None` and the loop continues before classification, so programs post as before.

### Notes (not blocking)
- **Mill-turn posted through a mill post** is judged as if the lathe post ran. A mill post has no work spindle, so this refuses too widely, never fails open. It blocks a milling-side program only on a mill-turn setup with a stated limit and a tool above it. Worth a follow-up issue, not a blocker.
- **Cohesion:** `section_spindle` lives in camcraft-post with app reading it (allowed direction), with a provenance line. `setup_workholding.rs` is about 175 lines. The heavy-lane test is `#[ignore]`d with its lane named.
- The decision file's "Open" paragraph should reflect point 1 once it is decided.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

### What I built, ran and tried
Head c08685ea trial-merged with origin/main 62a2c93a (includes #1202; clean, local only, never pushed). The PR-only diff is `setup_workholding.rs`, `posting.rs`, `posting_mounts.rs`, `posting_per_op.rs`, `post/dialect.rs`, three test suites and the decision file. **No golden, recorded stream or `post/mod.rs` change** (`git diff origin/main HEAD --stat` over `crates/*/tests/golden`, `crates/post/tests/recorded` and `post/mod.rs` is empty), so the stream is main's.

|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-post` (every binary + lib) | all pass (lib 27, recorded_streams 12, script_fanuc_lathe 15, each dialect 11, post_engine 33, ...) |
| lathe_workholding_kinds | 10 passed, 1 ignored (heavy lane, named) |

Throwaway probe (local test, deleted): a revolved Ø12 bar, Setup1 with a workholding max of 2000 rpm, through `posting::post_script` with fanuc-lathe, tormach-lathe, fanuc (mill) and haas (mill), across machine kinds none / mill / lathe / mill-turn.

### Requested before merge
1. **A turning operation on a mill-turn, posted through a milling post, is no longer held to the chuck limit, and it posts.** `crates/app/src/setup_workholding.rs`, `work_speed`: `(WorkVoice::ToolSpindle, _) => WorkSpeed::Not`, widened only for `Kind::Lathe`. Reproduction: machine `kind: "mill-turn"`, Facing op F1 (insert TN-1600-0R8 at 3000 rpm, z 16 -> 14 on a solid bar), chuck limit 2000:
   - fanuc-lathe / tormach-lathe: refused, `D1: turns the work at 3000 rpm (G97), over ... 2000 rpm` (correct).
   - **fanuc.cps: POSTED, `S3000 M3`; haas.cps: POSTED, `S3000 M3`.** The gate is silent.

   On main this was refused, whatever the post: the old clause judged every `spindle_law::turns` op, and every Turn-family kind counts. So the PR now lets through a case main stopped, in the dangerous direction. "A mill post's S drives the tool spindle" holds on a mill. On a mill-turn, `M3` is the main (work) spindle on many controls. Either way, a facing or turning path only cuts if the work turns, so a turning section posted at the tool's rpm has to be judged against the chuck. Fix, smallest first:
   - (a) on `Lathe | MillTurn`, `(ToolSpindle, Some(LatheVoice::WorkSpindle))` -> `Stated`, the same widening the PR already gives a plain lathe. It is strict for an on-centre drill on a mill-turn through a mill post, which is the safe side.
   - (b) or a door that refuses a turning kind through a milling post by name.

   Pin it with this reproduction (fanuc.cps, mill-turn, Facing 3000 over 2000 -> refused; at 2000 -> posts).

### Checked and holding
- **Dialect reading:** `work_voice` reads the `capabilities` mask (turning bit -> WorkSpindle, milling only -> ToolSpindle, none/0/negative/NaN/unparsed-as-absent -> Undeclared, a script that fails to load -> error). `speaks_turning` is now `== WorkSpindle`, so the lathe door and the gate read one mask. Its unit pins cover the shipped fanuc-lathe, tormach-lathe and fanuc.
- **Which script is judged:** the one that runs. `post_script_body` and `post_each` with an explicit script judge every op by that script's dialect. The gate view and the per-mount / per-op posts read each op's own setup post (`mounted_voices`, cached per `PostRef`). An unreadable script reads as Undeclared, the strict side.
- **Lathe post, any machine:** on-centre Drill 8000 / 2000 refused with no machine, a mill, a mill-turn and a lathe. Facing 3000 / 2000 refused on lathe and mill-turn; at 4000 it posts `G97 S3000 M03`. `Refused` sections (milling kinds, off-centre or tilted drill, probe) are not judged because `lathe_voice::at_post` refuses them by name first. It runs on all three post paths (`posting.rs:457`, `posting_mounts.rs:210`, `posting_per_op.rs:124`).
- **Mill post on a plain lathe:** judged like an undeclared script (facing and drill both refused). This only widens what is judged.
- **C sections:** max(C feed, C rapid)/360 vs the limit; no C rate -> refused by name (pins pass).
- **G96:** the clamp path is untouched. **No limit stated:** nothing judged, programs unchanged.
- **Boundary text:** `shown()` prints one decimal only when whole rpm would print both numbers the same ("2000.4 ... 2000.0"). That fixes my earlier cosmetic note.

### Notes (not blocking)
- A mill-family on-centre drill on a mill-turn or a mill through a milling post (`S8000 M3`) is still not judged. That was also unjudged on main, so it is not a regression; fix (a) above covers the mill-turn case.
- `setup_workholding.rs` is 232 lines and `dialect.rs` 141. The heavy-lane test's ignore reason names its lane.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Judging chosen over a door - it only adds a refusal over the limit. The third review's blocker is fixed. On a lathe or mill-turn, a section that turns the work (a turning kind or an on-centre drill) is now judged at its rpm through a milling post too. I found no remaining cell where a section that turns the chuck above the limit posts without a refusal, and no refusal that main gave and this head drops (apart from the cross drill, which the issue asks to free).

### What I built, ran and tried
Head 30e350fd already contains origin/main 62a2c93a (the trial merge was a no-op). Built locally; nothing was pushed. **Goldens, recorded streams and `post/mod.rs` are untouched** (`git diff origin/main HEAD --stat` over `crates/*/tests/golden`, `crates/post/tests/recorded`, `crates/post/src/post/mod.rs` is empty), so the stream every post reads is main's.

I also printed the cell walk (`every_machine_dialect_and_section_cell_gives_its_verdict -- --nocapture`). I ran a throwaway probe (deleted) of an off-centre and an on-centre Drill on a lathe and a mill-turn through fanuc-lathe, fanuc and haas.

### `work_speed` checked arm by arm
| Post voice | Section (`lathe_voice::voice_of`) | Machine | Verdict | Who stops it above the limit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| any | none (no path) | any | not judged | the post refuses an ungenerated op |
| turning | WorkSpindle | any (none / mill included) | rpm judged | workholding clause |
| turning | LiveTool | any | C rate judged (no C rate -> refused) | workholding clause |
| turning | Refused | any | not judged | the lathe door (`at_post`, on all three post paths) |
| milling | WorkSpindle | lathe, mill-turn | rpm judged | workholding clause (the fix) |
| milling | WorkSpindle | mill, none | not judged | no chuck on that spindle; Turn kinds cannot be created there (family door), so only an on-centre mill drill lands here |
| milling | LiveTool | lathe, mill-turn | C rate judged | workholding clause |
| milling | LiveTool | mill, none | not judged | the engine refuses `PARAM LiveTool` for a script without `liveTooling` |
| milling | Refused | lathe | rpm judged | workholding clause |
| milling | Refused | mill-turn, mill, none | not judged | milling section on the tool spindle |
| undeclared | any section | any | judged (rpm, or C rate) | workholding clause (the strict reading, #1199) |

**Against main:** main judged every Turn-family op (any machine, any post) and every Drill on a plain lathe. Here:
- **Turn ops:** judged under every voice on a lathe or mill-turn. On a mill or with no machine they cannot be created.
- **Lathe drills:** on-centre ones are WorkSpindle, judged under every voice. Off-centre or tilted ones are Refused: the door stops them under a turning post, and they are judged under a milling or undeclared post. My probe could not even generate an off-centre axial drill on a plain lathe.
- **The one refusal dropped:** main's false judgement of a cross drill on a mill-turn, which is the issue's done-means.

### Does the table test exercise every cell?
24 combinations are walked (4 machines x 3 voices x 2 sections). **15 are asserted; 9 are skipped as "not creatable on this machine"**: Work on none / mill (Facing is turning work), and Tool (mill Face) on a plain lathe. Those skips match the family door, but the test does not assert why it skipped. The `judged()` oracle's `("milling", Tool) => kind == "lathe"` row is therefore never reached. That arm (`ToolSpindle + Refused + Lathe -> Stated`) keeps a main refusal and has no pin. It is not blocking: the arm only adds refusals, and getting a Refused section onto a plain lathe needs a remount. Notes below.

### Notes (not blocking)
1. **Skipped cells:** in `every_machine_dialect_and_section_cell_gives_its_verdict`, assert the skip reason for the 9 skipped cells (the `CreateOperation` refusal names the family). Pin the `ToolSpindle + Refused + Lathe` arm with an op created on a mill-turn and remounted onto a lathe, or with an on-centre plus off-centre drill pair. A `P7` follow-up is enough.
2. **The author's doubt, C column only on a mill-turn:** on a plain lathe a C section goes through the same arm (`(_, LiveTool) -> OnC`), and a lathe stating no C rate is refused by name - the strict side. No pin needed.
3. **The author's doubt, on-centre drill through a milling post on a mill-turn is now judged:** that is the safe side. It refuses a fast axial live drill under a stated chuck limit, a legal program, only when the user both states a limit and posts a mill-turn through a milling post. Worth a `P7` issue if a user hits it; no pin beyond the existing ones.
4. **Milling sections on a mill-turn through a milling post** stay unjudged (`S8000 M3`). Main did not judge them either. This is correct as long as that control's M3 drives the tool spindle; a mill-turn whose M3 is the main spindle would need its own dialect. That belongs in the #1199 / mill-turn dialect discussion, not here.
5. `setup_workholding.rs` is 244 lines. No unwrap/expect outside tests. The refusal text prints a decimal when the two speeds would read the same.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
